title: The Acropolis morning
summary: The one unmissable sight, done early while everyone is fresh, then an easy afternoon on car-free streets.

stops.text: Be at the gate for opening: fewer people and cooler. Strollers are not allowed on the rock, so take a baby carrier. Allow 1.5 hours.
Coffee and a snack right below the Acropolis.
Flat floors and lifts, so the stroller works here. An hour is enough: the Caryatids and the top-floor Parthenon gallery.
Lunch nearby (or Arcadia or Yard, all on the same street).
Nap walk: push the stroller along the wide pedestrian street around the Acropolis (Dionysiou Areopagitou, then Apostolou Pavlou) towards Thissio.
The lower stone paths are shady and car-free, good for a toddler to walk. The summit is a short climb, easier with the carrier.

tips: If she walks on the Acropolis, hold her hand: the marble is polished and there are drops without railings.
There is no shade or food on the rock. Bring water and a hat.

title: Ancient Agora and the old town
summary: Ruins with grass and room to run, then the liveliest square in Athens.

stops.text: A big green site with gravel paths where she can roam safely. The rebuilt Stoa of Attalos has a small museum and shade.
Inside the same site, up a gentle path. The best-preserved Greek temple there is.
Street musicians, fruit stalls and the flea market lanes. Busy: keep her in the stroller or carrier here.
Lunch a minute from the square (Efcharis is next door). Feyrouz is a good quick alternative for savoury pies.
Nap walk through Plaka's quieter lanes. Expect some steps and cobbles; the carrier is easier than the stroller in upper Plaka.
Small and quick. The Tower of the Winds is the highlight and can be seen well from the fence if you would rather not go in.
Something sweet to finish.

tips: Monastiraki is the main spot for pickpockets. Keep bags zipped and in front of you.

title: Guards, garden and the marble stadium
summary: The most toddler-friendly day: soldiers, ducks, a playground and a running track.

stops.text: Syntagma Square: the guards in front of Parliament change on the hour. On Sundays the full parade is at 11:00. The pigeons are a show of their own.
Enter beside Parliament. Shady, flat paths, a duck pond, turtles and a playground. Let her set the pace.
Lunch close to the garden.
Nap walk through the garden to the Zappeion hall and on towards the stadium.
She can run on the track where the 1896 Olympics were held, and you can stand on the podium.
Fresh profiteroles on the way back.

tips: The stadium's upper tiers are steep with no railings; stay at track level with her.

title: Museums and the sunset hill
summary: A gentle indoor morning in Kolonaki, then the funicular up to the best view in Athens.

stops.place: Kotsanas Museum of Ancient Greek Technology
stops.text: Hands-on machines and moving models, so more fun with a small child than glass cases. Or choose the Museum of Cycladic Art nearby.
Optional: skip the galleries and go straight to the rooftop cafe for lunch with a view over the garden.
Nap in the stroller or back at your room.
Take a taxi to the funicular station in Kolonaki (the streets up to it are steep with many steps). Ride up for sunset over the Acropolis and the sea.

tips: There are steps at the top of Lycabettus. Take the carrier, not the stroller.
In November the sun sets a little after 17:00, and it is windy and cooler at the top.

title: Sea air at the Niarchos park
summary: A break from ruins: lawns, a big playground and a view of the sea, 15 minutes by taxi from the centre.

stops.text: Start at the playgrounds, then walk the gentle slope up to the top of the hill for the view: sea on one side, Acropolis on the other. Fully stroller-friendly.
Lunch at one of the cafes in the centre, or bring a picnic for the lawn.
Nap in the stroller along the canal, or head back.
Optional: Flisvos Marina, 10 minutes further by taxi, has a seafront promenade, yachts to look at and another playground.

tips: Good choice for the day after a long sightseeing day.

title: Rainy day
summary: Keep this one in your pocket. November has some wet days.

stops.text: Huge and stroller-friendly. Pick three things rather than everything: the gold Mask of Agamemnon, the bronze Zeus or Poseidon, and the Antikythera mechanism.
Lunch a few minutes' walk away.
After the nap: a calm, modern museum that takes about an hour. Van Gogh, Monet and Picasso.

tips: The Acropolis Museum is the other good rainy-day option if you have not been yet.

title: Cape Sounion and the coast
summary: The Temple of Poseidon on a cliff above the sea, about 1.5 hours' drive along the coast. Half a day.

stops.text: Leave after lunch so she naps in the car on the way. Go by rental car or a pre-booked taxi, and ask for a child seat in advance.
Temple of Poseidon. A short walk from the car park on uneven ground. Lord Byron carved his name on one of the columns.
Stay for the light before sunset, then drive back along the coast road.

tips: It is very windy on the cape: bring a warm layer for her.
The cliffs are unfenced in places. Carrier or hand-holding the whole time.

title: Aegina island
summary: A real Greek island as a day trip: a harbour town, fishing boats and pistachios.

stops.text: Ferry from Piraeus port (metro or taxi from the centre). The slower car ferry takes about 75 minutes and has decks and space for her to walk; the fast boat takes about 40 but you stay seated.
Aegina town: walk the waterfront, watch the boats, buy pistachios, which the island is famous for.
Fish lunch at the harbour.
Optional: taxi to the Temple of Aphaia, a beautiful hilltop temple (about 25 minutes each way). Otherwise an easy afternoon in town.
Ferry back.

tips: Check the return ferry times when you arrive; there are fewer boats in winter.
Skip this one if the sea is rough.

title: A day for her: the zoo
summary: Attica Zoological Park, near the airport, about 40 minutes by taxi. Large, flat and made for small children.

stops.text: Arrive at opening and start with the birds and the farm animals.
Lunch at the zoo cafe.
She will probably fall asleep in the stroller; finish the loop and head back.

tips: Works well as a last-day plan if you have a late flight: it is 15 minutes from the airport.
